subject: Critical Thinking
title: Moral Exemplars: Learning Ethics from Real People
description: A 60-second lesson on Moral Exemplars: Learning Ethics from Real People.

hook.text: You don't learn courage from a textbook. You learn it from watching someone be brave.

buildup.text: Moral exemplars: people whose lives embody virtues so clearly that they become models for others.

discovery.text: Aristotle: 'We become what we repeatedly do.' But we first need to see what virtue looks like.

twist.text: Heroes are flawed. Gandhi was harsh to his family. Mandela had a violent past.

climax.text: The modern crisis: social media creates false exemplars. True moral exemplars are often quiet, unphotogenic, & unknown.

punchline.text: You don't need a perfect hero. You need a real one.

quiz.question: Why does virtue ethics emphasize moral exemplars?
options: Because virtue is learned through observing and emulating people who embody it
To create a list of rules

details.summary: Moral exemplars are individuals whose lives embody ethical excellence, providing concrete models of virtue in action. Studying them offers practical moral guidance that abstract theories alone cannot deliver.
details.whyItMatters: Real examples of moral courage and integrity inspire people more effectively than philosophical arguments and make ethical ideals tangible.
takeaways: Exemplars make abstract virtues concrete and imitable
Studying moral exemplars bridges theory and practice
Different cultures highlight different moral heroes

faq.question: Why are moral exemplars important for ethical development?
faq.answer: They provide living proof that ethical ideals are achievable, not just theoretical abstractions. Seeing courage or generosity in action motivates imitation.

faq.question: Can flawed individuals still serve as moral exemplars?
faq.answer: Yes. Exemplars need not be perfect. Their specific virtuous actions can inspire even if other aspects of their character are imperfect.
